description: Killing parrots crashes your game. Note: I did kill other mobs and it isn t just swinging the sword and i got the same result everytime i killed a parrot. 19w40a: [ crash-2019-10-03_20.30.29-client.txt] Description: Unexpected error java.lang.NullPointerException: Unexpected error at atd.a(SourceFile:407) at axx.f(SourceFile:1234) at dmq.a(SourceFile:363) at das.aE(SourceFile:1234) at das.aG(SourceFile:1517) at das.n(SourceFile:1367) at das.d(SourceFile:907) at das.b(SourceFile:569) at net.minecraft.client.main.Main.main(SourceFile:199)
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft Java Edition 19w40a.
2. Create a new Singleplayer world with default settings.
3. Attack a parrot in the game.
4. Observe that the game crashes with a `java.lang.NullPointerException` error.
5. Repeat steps 3-4 multiple times to confirm the crash occurs each time a parrot is attacked.
Observed Behavior:
When a player attacks and kills a parrot in Minecraft version 19w40a, the game crashes, resulting in a java.lang.NullPointerException. This crash occurs consistently every time a parrot is killed, regardless of the weapon used or whether the player has attacked other types of mobs without issue. The error log indicates that the crash originates from an unexpected null reference within the game's code during the execution of the attack sequence on the parrot. The specific stack trace shows the error occurring at `atd.a(SourceFile:407)`, followed by several other method calls leading up to the main game loop. 

This issue is critical as it prevents players from interacting with parrots without crashing the game, affecting gameplay experience and functionality. The crash report filename is `crash-2019-10-03_20.30.29-client.txt`, which can be referenced for further investigation. Players have confirmed that this bug is not isolated to a specific weapon or attack method, as all attempts to kill parrots result in the same crash.
Expected Behavior: When a player attacks a parrot, the game should allow the action to complete without crashing, resulting in the parrot being damaged or killed as intended, while the player remains in control of the game. There should be no unexpected errors or exceptions, ensuring a smooth gameplay experience similar to interactions with other mobs. This behavior should be consistent across all game versions.
